ARCHIVED, SO 3408, Rescission of Secretary's Order 3368

status_summary: Secretary's Order 3433, signed 2025-06-23 and effective immediately, rescinds Order 3408 of 2022 in full and reinstates, with updates, Order 3368 of 2018. It directs the Solicitor's office and the Chief Information Officer to maintain a public Litigation Transparency Portal, post within 30 days a searchable list of consent decrees and settlements since fiscal year 2012 with associated attorneys' fee payments, and post final agreements within 15 days of execution. Whether the portal is live and populated was not confirmed.

timeline.event: Interior issued Secretary's Order 3433, which rescinds Order 3408, reinstates Order 3368 with updates, and directs a public Litigation Transparency Portal listing consent decrees, settlements and attorneys' fee payments.

title: Reinstate the Interior policy on open access to litigation settlements and fees
uncertainties: In review the signed order was opened on doi.gov and read: section 5 rescinds Order 3408, reinstates Order 3368 with updates, requires the Litigation Transparency Portal with case-level details including fees and their source, requires 30-day comment periods for qualifying proposed settlements and posting of final agreements within 15 days, and certification of fee payments over $10,000; section 6 allows written waivers that must themselves be posted. The archived page for Order 3408 says it was canceled and replaced by Order 3433. Whether the portal has been published and populated was not confirmed; two web searches did not surface it. The order creates no enforceable rights and can be revoked by a later Secretary.
